html:
The Iranian Revolution overthrew the monarchy of Mohammad Reza Shah in 1979 and replaced it with an Islamic Republic led by the cleric Ruhollah Khomeini.

The Shah had used oil wealth to modernise Iran fast, through the White Revolution and lavish projects, but he ruled through a feared secret police, SAVAK, and depended on the United States. Inflation, inequality and offence to religion turned merchants, students, workers, leftists and the Shia clergy against him.

Protests began in January 1978 and grew through a cycle of mourning marches every forty days. Strikes shut the oil industry. The Shah left in January 1979. Khomeini returned from exile in Paris on 1 February to millions in the streets, and the army stood aside ten days later. A referendum in April created the Islamic Republic.

Khomeini's followers soon pushed aside liberal and leftist allies. In November students seized the US embassy and held its staff for 444 days. In 1980 Saddam Hussein invaded, starting the Iran-Iraq War. The revolution inspired Islamists far beyond Iran; the same year saw the Grand Mosque seizure.
sum: The Iranian Revolution overthrew the monarchy of Mohammad Reza Shah in 1979 and replaced it with an Islamic Republic led by the cleric Ruhollah Khomeini.
